input.question: Which is the adaptive value about our organs facing one specific direction ?
input.ground_truth: > Situs inversus is found in about 0.01% of the population, or about 1 person in 10,000. Most people with situs inversus have no medical symptoms or complications resulting from the condition You kind of answered your own question a little. The simple answer is that there is no advantage. There is a lot more than you might expect that has no adaptive advantage at all. It's just a product of evolutionary history. If the arrangement can be reversed and there are no medical problems that result, then the reasonable conclusion is that there is no adaptive advantage. The organs are arranged as they are because of developmental processes that are left over probably from the earliest vertebrates.
